Support for OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol.

## Changes

- **GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are built-in models.**
  - `gpt-6.2-astra` and `gpt-6.2-sol` are on the Codex model list, so they show in `/v1/models` and the forgiving names find them (`gpt-6-2-sol`, `openai/gpt-6-2-astra`).
  - Fusebox already sent any `gpt-` model to Codex accounts. Before this release their requests were not priced.
- **Prices for both models,** from OpenAI's pricing page, in the rate card `2026-11-18.1` and the default catalogue `t3-2026-11-18.1`:

  | Per million tokens | Input | Cached input | Cache write (30 min / 12 h) | Output |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | GPT-6.2 Astra | $8 | $0.40 | $10 / $20 | $40 |
  | GPT-6.2 Sol | $2 | $0.10 | $2.50 / $5 | $10 |

  - Above 272K input tokens, input and cache rates double and output is 1.5 times as much (rate card only; the default catalogue is flat, as before).
  - Batch is half price and Fast is double. Flex is not offered for these models.
  - Ultrafast costs three times Standard until 28 February 2027 and six times from 1 March 2027, OpenAI's launch price. Fusebox switches by itself on that date (at midnight UTC, eight hours before OpenAI does).
  - Requests already stored for these models are priced at the next start.
- **Thinking turned off asks for low effort** on GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra. These models take `low` to `max`; OpenAI rejects `none` and `minimal`, so a translated request with thinking off (or `minimal`) failed before. Other models are unchanged.

## Upgrading

- **Database.** No change; the usage database stays on schema 5.
- **No new settings** and no API changes.
- **Prices:** two new rows, no existing row changed. `scripts/update-usage-pricing.py` now keeps a fallback row's dates and uses OpenAI's 30-minute cache write rate when a row has no 5-minute one; this changes no existing row.

## Known issue

- **SQLite advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0459 ([#60](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/issues/60)).** Unchanged from v0.17.0.

Validation: 1,046 Rust tests (13 ignored), 193 dashboard tests and 59 Python tests passed, and formatting and Clippy passed on the model change; the Release workflow tests the tag on Linux, macOS and Windows. Running in production since 18 November 2026: both models listed, the new catalogue in use, no other change seen.

[Full comparison with v0.17.1](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.17.1...v0.17.2).
